[Discussion] Which aspects of your favorite video games are often exaggerated by fans and reviewers?

The difficulty in Dark Souls is often exaggerated. Yes, it's a hard game, but it's not terribly unfair aside from a few places. It simply requires the player to get better and learn the systems being used. Dark Souls isn't hard as much as it is uncompromising. You either learn it or you don't. If you don't, you don't progress. In a way, it's refreshing in that it respects the player in this way, instead of rubber-banding to let the player win so they don't miss out on the cool set-piece movie-scene ending, you have to earn it. And I like that.

I think that they discussed this problem on Previously Recorded. That is that part of the problem with modern titles like COD is that there is way too much hand holding that paradoxically just ends up killing the narrative rather than I think the intended purpose of adding to it. That instead of the player being a character interacting in a world the player is just there to perform certain prompted commands in order to progress the story along. And that this just serves to detract from the experience because as soon as you start doing this you essentially just kill immersion since at that point it becomes obvious that you're just playing a game - and a pretty poor one at that. This, I think, being the video game equivalent of a actor corpsing on stage I.E., killing both the illusion of the character and the world being created.

The example that they use in their Bloodborne video is of a tough monster protecting an alleyway with the gag that even if you defeat this monster there's actually nothing down the alleyway. This probably being put into the game to give the lesson that you don't have to kill every monster you see if there's the option to bypass them.

Anyway the point that I'm trying to make is that it seems to be not a problem over difficulty but rather narrative. That if you have to figure out how to kill a monster or how a mechanic of a game works then this provides more engagement to the story rather than having to wade through endless cut scenes or having the weakspots of the bosses highlighted for you, for example. The tragedy being that we've been so conditioned into games becoming glorified Skinner boxes - to the point where it has been normalized - that when a game comes along that actually gets the mechanics right in terms of telling a good story, I.E., actually having it integrated in game play like in the above example, it's seen as being hard when really it's just doing it's job better than what has become the accepted product, IMHO.

Jesus Christ people if you get stuck that's what Gamefaqs and Wikis are for: you don't have to have everything spoonfed you all the time.

I agree with you 100%. Some parts are too unforgiving, but for the most part you just have to learn game mechanics and it becomes very playable. Don't learn then gg.

The steps are fairly simple.

Open a Terminal and type:

gksu gedit /etc/apt/preferences.d/libreoffice-libreoffice-5-0.pref

Then in the New Windows that opens enter this code and save/close the document.

Package: *
Pin: release o=LP PPA-libreoffice-libreoffice-5-0
Pin-Priority: 701

Now in terminal enter the following code:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa-libreoffice/libreoffice-5-0
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get dist-upgrade

If you want to try the new Breeze Icon Theme for Libre Office 5 then also type:

sudo apt-get install libreoffice-style-breeze
